name: Cassava Mosaic Disease
description: A devastating viral disease of cassava causing distorted, yellow-mottled leaves and severe yield reduction. It is spread by whiteflies and through infected cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow or pale green mosaic pattern on leaves
Leaf distortion, curling, and reduced size
Stunted plant growth with shortened internodes
Plants may appear bushy with many weak stems
causes: Cassava mosaic geminivirus transmitted by whiteflies
Use of infected stem cuttings for planting
Whitefly populations spreading virus between plants
Presence of wild cassava relatives serving as reservoirs
treatments: No cure once plant is infected
Remove and burn severely infected plants
Use systemic insecticides to reduce whitefly populations
Roguing early-infected plants to reduce inoculum
prevention: Plant resistant cassava varieties (e.g., TME series)
Rogue out infected plants early in the season
Remove alternative host plants near fields
Practice field sanitation and clean planting tools
